posts.heading: September 27, 2026
posts.text:
The station was quieter than the previous week, with 234 feeder visits compared to an average of 288.9, and 17 species recorded against a seven-day average of 18.7. The auditory landscape remained stable at 296 detections, matching the weekly average of 296.7 despite the new c120-extra microphone added yesterday. Core residents such as the Tufted Titmouse, Carolina Chickadee, and Eastern Towhee held their ground, while the Red-bellied Woodpecker was absent for the first time in a week.

Visual activity was led by the Tufted Titmouse, which logged 85 visits, including a perch on the treat bowl feeder before sunrise. The Northern Cardinal was last seen just four minutes after sunset, extending the day’s activity into the evening. No new species were first heard or seen.

posts.heading: September 26, 2026
posts.text:
Yesterday recorded 17 species and 284 feeder visits, slightly below the recent baseline of 19.6 species and 278.7 visits. The Eastern Towhee, Carolina Chickadee, and Northern Cardinal dominated audio detections, while the Tufted Titmouse led in visual presence. A Rose-breasted Grosbeak returned after seven days away.

At 10:44, a second microphone began recording alongside the existing unit, expanding the station’s auditory range. No species were heard for the first time at this station under the new setup.

Visually, the Tufted Titmouse was active from 11 minutes before sunrise and the Northern Cardinal observed as late as 9 minutes after sunset. Mourning Doves were absent, breaking a week-long streak of daily presence. Seed and nectar feeders were recently refilled.

posts.heading: September 25, 2026
posts.text:
The station logged 266 visits and 22 species. Tufted Titmice and Carolina Chickadees remained the most frequent visitors, while Gray Catbird, Northern Flicker, and American Goldfinches were absent from the daily count.

Two feeders were refilled in the late afternoon, specifically the seed-feeder at 18:22 and the nectar-feeder at 18:38. House Finch and White-breasted Nuthatch were recorded daily for the past week.

A Northern Cardinal was visually confirmed 11 minutes before sunrise. By 19:03, a Blue Jay was observed 20 minutes before sunset.

posts.heading: September 24, 2026
posts.text:
The station was busier than the previous week's average, recording 360 visits against a weekly mean of 245.7 and detecting 19 species. Regulars such as Northern Cardinals, Carolina Chickadees, and Tufted Titmice remained consistent, appearing on every day of the last week. The visit count was driven largely by high-frequency sightings of Tufted Titmice and Ruby-throated Hummingbirds, which were seen 143 and 53 times respectively.

Several species marked their first confident visual record at the station, including the Common Grackle, which was also heard for the first time. An Eastern Kingbird returned after eight days away, last recorded on September 16. In contrast, the Eastern Phoebe, Downy Woodpecker, and Song Sparrow, all seen in the prior week, were not detected on this day.

The day began with a Northern Cardinal seen 10 minutes after sunrise and ended with a Northern Cardinal seen 11 minutes before sunset. The total of 16 species heard aligns with the pattern of consistent core species and sporadic additions like the Northern Flicker and Canada Goose.

posts.heading: September 23, 2026
posts.text:
Yesterday was a busier day for the station than the recent trend, with 321 feeder visits and 19 species recorded. These totals stand out against the past week's average of 234.7 visits and 18.4 species. The station saw a full complement of regulars, including the Tufted Titmouse, Carolina Chickadee, and Northern Cardinal, which all visited the feeder multiple times.

The audio logs captured a broad range of vocalizations, with the Carolina Chickadee and Northern Cardinal detected most frequently. Several species that were absent earlier in the week, such as the Eastern Phoebe and Red-shouldered Hawk, were heard yesterday.

Visual records confirmed the presence of familiar regulars like the House Finch and Blue Jay, as well as the Mourning Dove. A Tufted Titmouse was also observed perching on the rim of a treat bowl during its visits.

posts.heading: September 22, 2026
posts.text:
Feeder traffic more than doubled the daily average of the past week, totaling 428 visits despite a drop in species count to 18. Tufted Titmice logged 203 visits. Visual observations remained strong for Northern Cardinals and Carolina Chickadees.

Carolina Wrens led the soundscape with 68 detections, followed by Northern Cardinals and Eastern Towhees. Eastern Towhees were particularly active during the midday hours. A Cedar Waxwing returned after a seven-day absence.

Eastern Phoebes and Downy Woodpeckers, present earlier in the week, were missing from today's log.

posts.heading: September 21, 2026
posts.text: The station recorded 124 feeder visits, compared to the recent weekly average of 230. The species count dipped to 18 from the mean of 20. Tufted Titmice were the most frequent visitors, seen 64 times, with Carolina Chickadees and Northern Cardinals following at 14 and 11 visits respectively. American Crows, Carolina Wrens, and Northern Cardinals provided the bulk of vocal detections. The day concluded with a Tufted Titmouse visiting 21 minutes before sunset, following its arrival 12 minutes before sunrise.
